subject: Proposal: commitment tiers & staggered ramp for SignalBridge dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@signalbridge.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity options for SignalBridge — initial proposal

Alex — attaching a first-pass dedicated capacity proposal and a small TCO workbook so you can see unit economics across ramp patterns. High-level summary below (also in the PDF):

Option 1 — Entry lane (50 GPU slate)
- Baseline: 50 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved
- Min gateway (soft floor): 10 GPUs kept warm for immediate low-latency requests
- Ramp: 50 -> 100 over 3 months based on usage triggers
- Recommended for ML inference where batch/throughput are moderate but latency matters

Option 2 — Mid (100 GPU slate)
- Baseline: 100 GPUs reserved
- Min gateway: 25 GPUs warm
- Ramp: 100 -> 150 over 2 months with burst capacity for peak experiments
- Better for teams with heavier QPS and larger KV cache targets

Option 3 — Performance (200 GPU slate)
- Baseline: 200 GPUs reserved with warm-standby region for failover
- Min gateway: 50 GPUs warm
- Ramp: staged over 4 months with canary rollout for models and autoscaling thresholds
- Includes optional dedicated prewarm credits and extended SLA (SLA addendum required)

Key toggles that materially affect unit economics: batching policy, KV cache hit rate, quantization profile, and allowed burst windows. See tab "Assumptions" in the attached XLSX.

Next steps I recommend: 1) review the attached TCO and highlight which usage curve (Low / Mid / High) best matches your forecast, 2) pick an option and identify any required compliance addenda, 3) quick sync to align contract cadence.

Attachments: [Attachment: SignalBridge_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: SB_Capacity_TCO_Scenarios.xlsx (XLSX)]

—Rachel

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options for SignalBridge — initial proposal

Alex — good questions, answers inline below. Quoting your numbered points for clarity.

1) Min gateway billing: the warm gateway GPUs are reserved (included in the committed pool) and priced at the same reservation rate; however we offer an optional warm-credit discount for the first quarter to reduce upfront burn while you validate integration. The attached XLSX has the two variants (standard reservation vs reservation + warm-credit).

2) Warm-standby region: for Option 3 we recommend full model warm copies (weights + optimized kernels + warmed KV snapshot) in the secondary region so failover is sub-second for the active set. Cross-region replication scope can be limited to the hot model shards to reduce cross-region traffic — we call this "hot-shard replicate" in the proposal.

3) 12-month blended: attached spreadsheet includes a "Quantized_8bit" tab with blended cost scenarios. Short answer: Option 2 (100 GPUs) with 8-bit quant yields ~23% lower token cost vs Option 3 (200 GPUs) because of utilization differences; Option 3 delivers higher headroom and lower risk of throttling but higher committed monthly burn. I pasted a quick extract below: 

- Option 2 (100 GPU), quantized target: ~$72k/month blended
- Option 3 (200 GPU), quantized target: ~$130k/month blended (includes warm-standby incremental)

If useful, we can produce a third sheet that maps your internal traffic S-curves to the exact activation months — happy to run that.

Next step: Karthik and Marissa, can we offer SignalBridge a short 4-week prewarm credit on Option 2 to accelerate adoption? I can draft the addendum.

—Rachel
